introducoes.uso: FeatherSlide is a presentation program that runs entirely on your machine: no account, no login, none of your content leaves it. Here is how to use each part, from creating slides to presenting in full screen. Follow in order with the arrow, or pick a topic in the side menu.
introducoes.atalhos: The keys that make the work faster. Slide and element keys work with the slide in focus; file and window keys work anywhere.

corpo: On the home page, choose New presentation or Open. A new presentation starts with a title slide.
• The home page also has 24 ready-made templates with sample slides: class, training, weekly meeting, report, case study, thesis defense, event, pitch, high contrast and more.
• The slide panel is on the left; the slide being edited in the middle; the speaker notes below.
• The ribbon on top has the Home, Insert, Design, Transitions, Animations, Slide Show and View tabs. Double-click a tab (or Ctrl+F1) to swap the ribbon for menus.
• Commands marked "Coming soon" do not work yet: each tooltip says what it will do.
New slide (Ctrl+M) adds a Title and content slide after the current one; the button arrow picks another layout.
• Layout changes the arrangement of the current slide and keeps the text already in the boxes.
• In the left panel: click to go to a slide, drag to reorder, right-click to duplicate, delete or hide.
• A hidden slide stays in the file, but the slide show skips it.
Click an element to select it; Shift+click adds another; dragging on the background selects what ends up inside.
• Drag to move; the corner and side handles resize. The arrow keys move 1 pt (10 pt with Shift).
• Delete removes, Ctrl+D duplicates, Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V copy and paste with the style.
• Arrange ▸ Align: pick To slide (aligns with the slide) or To selection (aligns the selected items with each other, two or more); Distribute needs three or more. Group is next to it.
Double-click a box (or press Enter with it selected) to type. Esc or a click outside finishes.
• Empty layout boxes show a gray hint that does not appear in the slide show.
• Font, size, color, bold, italic, underline and alignment apply to all the text of the selected box.
• Line breaks use the real letter widths (Liberation Sans/Arial and Liberation Serif/Times, the same as the PDF): text breaks on the same lines on screen and in the PDF.
Insert → Shapes puts a rectangle, ellipse, triangle, arrow or line in the middle of the slide.
• Fill and Outline (Home → Drawing) pick the colors; Weight, the outline thickness.
• Insert → Image embeds the image in the presentation: the .fsdz carries it along.
• Insert → Chart: column, bar, line, area, pie and doughnut. Double-click the chart to edit its data; the type can also be changed in the data window.

• Table: copy cells in FeatherSheet or Excel and paste (Ctrl+V) on the slide: it becomes a table. With the table selected, Insert → Table style picks the color and turns on banded rows, bold first column and a total row.
F5 starts from the first slide; Shift+F5, from the current slide.
Slide Show → Rehearse timings: presents from the start and measures how long each slide stays up; on leaving (Esc), the times become each slide's automatic advance. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
View → Reading mode: presents inside the window, without full screen, to show it in a video call.
View → Outline: the presentation as text. One title per line and the body below it, with Tab. Apply changes the slides (extra titles become new slides; none is deleted).

Insert → Date and time or Slide number: opens Header and footer. The date, slide number and a text show at the bottom of every slide and update by themselves (the number changes when slides move). You can hide them on the title slide. "Start at" sets the number of the first slide (0 so the cover does not count).
Animations → Exit: the chosen effect plays backwards and the element leaves the slide. Before the click it is on screen. Each element has one animation: entrance or exit.
• Advance with →, Space, Enter or a click; go back with ← or Backspace. Home and End go to the first and the last. Type a slide number and Enter to jump straight to it.
• Esc leaves the slide show.
The presentation is saved as .fsdz: a container with the slides in Arrow columns and the images as files.

• Open also reads .pptx (PowerPoint and Google Slides) and .odp (LibreOffice Impress): slides, boxes, shapes, images, tables (from .pptx), shape links (including "go to slide"), rotated shapes, background and notes, at the file's own slide size (16:10, A4 and others are not stretched) and with the file's embedded fonts, so text wraps on the same lines. On save, the presentation becomes .fsdz (the original is not touched).

• To send to someone on PowerPoint or Google Slides: the Export as PowerPoint (.pptx) button on the top bar. Slides, text boxes, shapes, photos, tables, charts, background and notes go along; icons, WordArt and freehand drawings are still left out (the status bar says how many).
• Each text box keeps the inner margin from the .pptx file (zero margin included), and it is stored in the .fsdz.
• Each time the presentation is saved (autosave included), the previous version goes to Version history, under Files; the 20 most recent are kept.
• Recovery keeps the drafts that were never saved (and a copy of any deleted file), newest first. Click one to pick up where you left off; Discard removes a draft (or all of them) after you confirm.
• Ctrl+S saves to the same file; Ctrl+Shift+S asks where.
• In the browser (development mode), Save downloads the file.
The gear in the top corner opens Settings: theme, color scheme, accent color, language and shortcuts.
• F12 opens the Monitor: memory, processor and graphics card, the console and the metrics of each engine command.
